parsed.study_design: Mixed-methods case study with household survey, environmental assessment, policy review, and simulation/sensitivity analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents and households of Southlea Park, a low-income peri-urban settlement in Harare; household survey n=150, supplemented by environmental assessments and stakeholder interviews
parsed.exposure: Local governance and institutional conditions for decentralized greywater services, measured through policy readiness, governance, finance, equity, monitoring, risk-management, and maintenance indicators under the Greywater Service Innovation Ladder
parsed.outcome: Baseline and simulated greywater service maturity and progression, including affordability, health protection, service reliability, equity safeguards, and readiness to transition from household-level practices to community and micro-utility service delivery
parsed.rationale: Section 3.4 (pp. 527–528) identifies an empirical Southlea Park case study using 150 household surveys, environmental assessments, policy-document analysis, and stakeholder interviews. Sections 4.1–4.3 (pp. 533–534) report observed baseline affordability, health-protection, reliability, and governance indices and simulate how institutional reforms affect progression to community and utility-grade greywater services. The population, governance exposure, sanitation-service outcomes, and mixed-methods case-study design are sufficiently identifiable.
